nodes.norm_label: downgrade-only quality governor (display-cadence budget, learned tier)

nodes.label: Render on demand
nodes.rationale: A paused, idle app draws nothing; Live 1x redraws about twice a second when the snapshot goes stale.

nodes.label: R5: No per-frame allocation

nodes.norm_label: r6: shader fragments end with tonemapping/colorspace includes

nodes.norm_label: moon made astrometric (annual aberration removed from the geometric moon)
nodes.rationale: The raw Moon sat ~20 arcsec off against the Sun and stars; corrected Sun-Moon separations are the apparent ones (9.2 arcsec at Luxor 2027-08-02, not 19).

nodes.rationale: Obscuration, sky-view discs, flare and panel share the same two discs; before, drawn discs reached totality 35 s late at Luxor and the panel could read Partial 100.0%.

nodes.label: Solar system to scale with one linear scale (orrery)
nodes.community_name: The astronomy behind Planet Location Marker (ASTRONOMY.md)
nodes.norm_label: solar system to scale with one linear scale (orrery)
nodes.rationale: A log scale was rejected: it bends Earth-to-planet lines away from true directions, so Mars would no longer be in Leo on the orrery while its beam says it is.

nodes.label: Static sky, moving Earth (equatorial grid drawn of date)
nodes.community_name: The astronomy behind Planet Location Marker (ASTRONOMY.md)
nodes.norm_label: static sky, moving earth (equatorial grid drawn of date)
nodes.rationale: Stars are placed once in J2000; precession and nutation appear because the Earth's axis moves inside the fixed sky. Exceptions: proper motion of fast stars and the of-date equatorial grid.

nodes.label: Sun angular radius at the live distance (not a constant 960 arcsec)
nodes.community_name: The astronomy behind Planet Location Marker (ASTRONOMY.md)
nodes.norm_label: sun angular radius at the live distance (not a constant 960 arcsec)
nodes.rationale: The constant 960 arcsec drew the 2027-08-02 umbra about 19% too narrow (104 km instead of 129 km half-width).

nodes.label: Totality's star limit in magnitudes (about 2.0)
nodes.community_name: The astronomy behind Planet Location Marker (ASTRONOMY.md)
nodes.rationale: Specified in magnitudes so every tier shows the same stars; the old exposure term reached magnitude 5.7 on High and started 2.8 min before second contact.

nodes.rationale: Keeps the satellites' orbital elements fresh without committing anything: fresh TLEs go only into the staged site, the committed copy is the fallback, a CelesTrak outage must not stop the deploy (continue-on-error), and a scheduled run redeploys only a commit CI passed on.

nodes.rationale: Layering and hygiene invariants are enforced by repo tests so they cannot silently regress.

nodes.label: No per-frame allocation of geometries, materials, textures or typed arrays
nodes.norm_label: no per-frame allocation of geometries, materials, textures or typed arrays

nodes.label: Pure modules rule (js/astro, js/core, js/geo, js/data: no three, DOM or window)
nodes.norm_label: pure modules rule (js/astro, js/core, js/geo, js/data: no three, dom or window)
nodes.rationale: Keeps astronomy and state testable in Node and usable from the worker; only core/prefs.js touches localStorage (guarded), and astronomy-engine is imported only through js/astro/ae.js by relative path.

nodes.label: Relative URLs only (no external URLs outside geocode.js and the About credits)

nodes.label: Shader rule: every ShaderMaterial fragment ends with tonemapping_fragment and colorspace_fragment

nodes.norm_label: user-visible strings rule (t()/tn()/n_() whole phrases, vietnamese in data/i18n/vi.json)
nodes.rationale: Whole phrases with {placeholders}, never fragments, keep translations grammatical; test/repo.i18n.test.mjs fails on missing, stale or placeholder-mismatched keys; machine formats (URL hash, .ics, diagnostics) stay unlocalized; the astro worker uses the table the client posts to it.

nodes.label: goldens job: render goldens with the pinned Chrome (workflow_dispatch)
nodes.norm_label: goldens job: render goldens with the pinned chrome (workflow_dispatch)
nodes.rationale: Goldens must come from the pinned Chrome on the CI runner, never from a developer machine; the 'goldens' artifact is unzipped into test/golden/ and committed.

nodes.label: Vendored-file and derived-texture hash checks (fetch-vendor / build-textures --check)
nodes.norm_label: vendored-file and derived-texture hash checks (fetch-vendor / build-textures --check)
nodes.rationale: CI checks hashes only: re-encoding textures is a deliberate, reviewed step because encoder output varies by Chrome version.

nodes.label: Offline reload through the service worker (staged site, sub-path)
nodes.norm_label: offline reload through the service worker (staged site, sub-path)
nodes.rationale: Checks the offline promise on the site exactly as pages.yml deploys it: the staged sw.js (content-hashed version) precaches from sw-manifest.json, then the page must reload offline from the worker alone.

nodes.label: Count-based performance gates (Low 1440x900, High 320x240, then a context loss)
nodes.norm_label: count-based performance gates (low 1440x900, high 320x240, then a context loss)
nodes.rationale: Counts, not milliseconds: shader programs and draw calls per tier, no frame drawn in 3 s while paused, twinkle at most 32/s under the 30 Hz cap, no getBoundingClientRect in a frame callback during a time-lapse; High runs at 320x240 so its frames come fast enough for the twinkle cap to matter.

nodes.label: Pinned Chrome for Testing build (CHROME_VERSION)
nodes.rationale: Every browser step runs one Chrome for Testing build because SwiftShader WebGL output is deterministic per build; test/golden/meta.json records the build the goldens were made with, so changing the pin makes the golden step skip with a notice until the goldens are rendered again.

nodes.label: Stage the site (site files only, sw-manifest.json, content-hashed sw.js version)
nodes.norm_label: stage the site (site files only, sw-manifest.json, content-hashed sw.js version)
nodes.rationale: A deploy that changes any file becomes a new service-worker version and an unchanged daily run does not; data/tle.json is outside the version hash (network-first), so a refresh needs no stamp.

nodes.norm_label: accuracy budget (about 1 arcminute 1800-2200; astrometric j2000 drawn, apparent positions in tables)
nodes.rationale: Beams and glyphs use astrometric J2000 so they line up with the star catalogue, while tables give apparent positions (of date, aberration, refraction); the difference is at most about 20 arcseconds plus refraction; outside 1800-2200 uncertain Delta T degrades accuracy and the app marks those years 'Reduced accuracy'.

nodes.label: Self-hosted, SHA-256-pinned vendoring (vendor/VENDOR.json, vendor/DERIVED.json)
nodes.rationale: Everything is served from the site and nothing is loaded from a CDN at run time; exact source URLs, versions and hashes (and each derived texture's source and recipe) are recorded and verifiable with --check.

nodes.rationale: The star catalogue is astrometric J2000 so beams land on the right stars; printed alt/az is what an observer measures. They differ by annual aberration (<=20.5 arcsec) and refraction.

nodes.rationale: The unit-sphere normal equals the WGS84 geodetic zenith Astronomy Engine uses, so altitudes match; cost is up to ~21 km in pin position.

nodes.rationale: Uncertainty in Delta T dominates far from the present: about a minute of time around 1000, tens of minutes toward 3000.
